name: TypeScript
description: Writing safer JavaScript with TypeScript's static type system, including interfaces, generics, unions and type narrowing.

questions.question: What happens to TypeScript type annotations when the code is compiled to JavaScript?
options: They are converted into runtime type checks
They are erased; the output JavaScript has no type annotations
They are kept as comments that browsers enforce
They cause a runtime error if types do not match
questions.explanation: TypeScript types exist only at compile time; they are removed during compilation and do not exist at runtime.

questions.question: What does the type annotation let id: string | number; allow?
options: id must be both a string and a number
id can only be a string
id can be either a string or a number
id can be any type
questions.explanation: The | operator creates a union type; the value can be any one of the member types.

questions.question: Why is 'unknown' generally safer than 'any'?
options: A value of type unknown must be narrowed (e.g. with typeof) before you can use it as a specific type
unknown values are checked at runtime
unknown can only hold primitive values
unknown disables type checking for the entire file
questions.explanation: any turns off type checking, while unknown forces you to prove the type before operating on the value.

questions.question: Given interface User { id: number; name: string; email: string }, what does Partial<User> produce?
options: A type with only the id property
A type where all properties are readonly
A type with all properties removed
A type where every property of User is optional
questions.explanation: Partial<T> is a built-in utility type that marks every property of T as optional.

questions.question: What is the type of the variable result in: function first<T>(arr: T[]): T | undefined { return arr[0]; } const result = first([1, 2, 3]);
options: any
number[]
number | undefined
unknown
questions.explanation: T is inferred as number from the argument, so the return type is number | undefined.

questions.question: In a discriminated union type Shape = { kind: 'circle'; r: number } | { kind: 'square'; size: number }, what lets TypeScript know shape.r is safe inside if (shape.kind === 'circle') { ... }?
options: TypeScript checks the value at runtime
Narrowing on the shared literal 'kind' property restricts the type to the circle member
The r property exists on both members
Type assertions are inserted automatically
questions.explanation: Comparing a literal discriminant property narrows the union to the matching member at compile time.

practical.title: Type a function with an interface
practical.instructions: Write a TypeScript interface Product with properties id (number), name (string) and price (number). Then write a function totalPrice that takes an array of Product and returns the sum of their prices as a number, with explicit parameter and return types.
practical.expected_output: interface Product { id: number; name: string; price: number; } function totalPrice(items: Product[]): number { return items.reduce((sum, p) => sum + p.price, 0); }

rubric.description: Declares the Product interface or type

rubric.hint: Give id and price the type number and name the type string.

rubric.description: Parameter typed as an array of Product
rubric.hint: Type the parameter as Product[] (or Array<Product>).
Annotate the return type: function totalPrice(items: Product[]): number { ... }.

tasks.title: Read the TypeScript Handbook basics
tasks.description: Read the Handbook sections on everyday types, narrowing and object types. Try each example in the TypeScript Playground.
tasks.completion_criteria: Can explain union types, interfaces, type aliases and narrowing with your own examples.

tasks.title: Convert a JavaScript file to TypeScript
tasks.description: Take a small JavaScript project, enable strict mode in tsconfig.json and convert files to .ts. Fix every type error without using any.
tasks.completion_criteria: tsc --noEmit runs with zero errors under strict mode and no explicit any.

tasks.title: Use generics and utility types
tasks.description: Write a generic typed API client function and a small in-memory repository class using generics. Use Partial, Pick, Omit and Record where appropriate.
tasks.completion_criteria: Code compiles under strict mode and uses at least one generic function, one generic class and three utility types.

tasks.title: Build a fully typed application
tasks.description: Build a small app (CLI or web) in strict TypeScript that models its domain with discriminated unions and validates external input at runtime before trusting it.
tasks.completion_criteria: Repository with strict tsconfig, discriminated unions, runtime validation and passing tests.
